title: Vitamin D for breastfed babies
summary: Many breastfed infants need a daily vitamin D supplement, formula often already has it.
whatsNormal:
Vitamin D supports bone health. Breast milk alone may not provide enough for some babies.

• AAP guidance: 400 IU vitamin D daily for breastfed or partially breastfed infants, starting soon after birth unless your clinician advises otherwise
• Standard infant formula is fortified, fully formula-fed babies may not need extra unless directed
• Drops are typical; give as your pediatrician or product label recommends
• Consistency matters more than perfect timing each day

If you combo-feed, ask your clinician whether supplementation is still needed.
watchFor: Giving adult or high-dose vitamin products not meant for infants
Missing doses for many days in a row, resume when you remember; do not double up without asking
Rash or vomiting after starting drops, uncommon but mention it
callDoctorIf: You are unsure which product or dose to use, your pediatrician can recommend a brand
Baby was premature or has special nutrition plan, follow NICU or specialist guidance
You want to discuss vitamin D in the context of your feeding plan
Any reaction you think is from the supplement
